Title: Celebrating Nurses on International Nurses Day
NewsSummary: A message for International Nurses Day by Dr Eunice Ndirangu, Dean at the Aga Khan School of Nursing and Midwifery, East Africa​
NewsContent:
A message for International Nurses Day by Dr Eunice Ndirangu, Dean at the Aga Khan School of Nursing and Midwifery, East Africa​

Welcome to 2020, the “Year of the Nurse and Midwife", a year to acknowledge the contribution of nurses and midwives to healthcare systems all over the world. Today as we celebrate International Nurses Day, I would like to appreciate nurses all over the world for their endless commitment to taking care of all of us, even during these uncertain times. At SONAM as we continue interacting with our students remotely, we remember that nurses are also responding to other non-COVID related illnesses through providing care for patients with pre-existing conditions and those requiring emergency care and routine services. Due to the pandemic, the world has recognised that nurses, as essential workers, are crucial to the survival and prosperity of humanity. As nurses, we see life and death, we see courage and hopelessness, we see fear and bravery and we see tragedy and success.

The theme for this year's International Nurses Day is “Nursing the world to health", which is very timely because of the health-related challenges we have faced so far. Nearly 200 years ago, Florence Nightingale demonstrated the invaluable role of handwashing and hygiene in disease prevention, reduction of mortality and morbidity. Today, nurses are driving these very principles in a bid to deal with the Covid-19 pandemic.

Thank you to all the nurses in the wards, communities, critical care units, in nursing homes, at home, in the labs, in private practice and wherever you are serving from. We appreciate your service, your leadership, your decision-making, your research and I urge governments and policymakers all over the world to support nurses in every way. Let us increase nursing jobs, enhance compensation, improve their working conditions and make it easier for nurses to do their jobs effectively. As you continue to nurse the world to health, do not forget to take care of yourselves as well. I wish you the very best as you mark this day with your families, workmates, patients and associations as you observe the various government directives. Remember that you are the backbone of our healthcare systems. We stand with you!
